issues.description: PerformanceWarning is raised as a hard exception, conflating warn and fail semantics
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass but is raised to abort the write. The class name lies about behavior, and the PR description itself asks whether raising is appropriate. Pick one identity: warnings.warn(...) and proceed, or rename to a real Error (e.g., ValueError) and raise. The test asserting pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...) currently locks in the wrong contract.

issues.description: Unreachable break immediately after raise PerformanceWarning is dead code
issues.detail: The `break` following `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` can never execute because the raise unwinds the stack. This signals the author had not decided whether the loop should fail-fast, collect-all, or warn-and-continue. Remove the dead statement and make the intended control flow explicit.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size uses max(1, itemsize), papering over an unstated invariant
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` defends against itemsize==0, a case that should not occur. Either assert the invariant and drop the max, or name the real case. Prefer `math.prod` (or `int(np.prod(...))`) to avoid numpy scalar leakage into the f-string message.

issues.description: Divisibility check inspects only dw[0] per axis, assuming uniform chunks
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks` can return ragged tail blocks, so checking only the first chunk per axis can silently miss misalignment on interior blocks. Either check every chunk on each axis, or state the invariant in a comment explaining why dw[0] is sufficient (e.g., interior chunks are uniform and only the remainder differs).

issues.description: `not x % y == 0` is hostile to readers; use `x % y != 0`
issues.detail: Operator precedence happens to make `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` mean the right thing, but the reader has to consult precedence rules to verify. Rewrite as `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:` — the meaning is immediate and the correctness check is obvious at a glance.

issues.description: Test name and assertion shape encode the warn/raise confusion as contract
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` asserts `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)` — the name says warns, the assertion requires an exception. Once the warn-vs-raise policy is decided (see P0), align the test: rename to `_raises` with `pytest.raises(ValueError)`, or switch to `pytest.warns(PerformanceWarning)`.

synthesis.summary: The core algorithmic idea — using zarr shard shape as `previous_chunks` so auto_chunks produces shard-aligned blocks — is sound, but the misalignment-detection block is not ready to land. The panel unanimously flags two P0 issues: PerformanceWarning is raised as a hard exception (a category error the PR description itself questions), and there is unreachable dead code (`break` after `raise`). The safe_chunk_size formula leans on a defensive `max(1, itemsize)` that masks an unstated invariant, and the per-axis divisibility check only inspects the first chunk, assuming uniform chunking that normalize_chunks does not guarantee. Decide the warn-vs-raise policy explicitly, fix the control flow, state the invariants, and update the test to match the chosen contract.
